module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 999

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/999](https://www.erdosproblems.com/999)
- [Er64b] Erdős, P., _Problems and results on diophantine approximations_. Compositio Math.
  (1964), 52-65.
- [KoMa20] Koukoulopoulos, Dimitris and Maynard, James, _On the Duffin-Schaeffer conjecture_.
  Ann. of Math. (2) (2020), 251--307.
-/

@[expose] public section

open MeasureTheory

namespace Erdos999

/-- `x` is *approximable* with respect to `f` if
$$\left\lvert x-\frac{p}{q}\right\rvert < \frac{f(q)}{q}$$
has infinitely many solutions with $(p,q)=1$. -/
def IsApproximable (f : ℕ → ℝ) (x : ℝ) : Prop :=
  {q : ℕ | 0 < q ∧ ∃ p : ℤ, Int.gcd p q = 1 ∧ |x - p / q| < f q / q}.Infinite

/--
For any function $f:\mathbb{N}\to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ the property that, for almost all
$\alpha$
$$\left\lvert \alpha-\frac{p}{q}\right\rvert < \frac{f(q)}{q}$$
has infinitely many solutions with $(p,q)=1$, is equivalent to
$$\sum_{q\geq 1}\phi(q)\frac{f(q)}{q}=\infty.$$

The Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture. It is easy to prove that the latter follows from the former.
Erdős proved this in the special case when $f(q)q$ is bounded. The full conjecture was proved by
Koukoulopoulos and Maynard [KoMa20].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_999 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ f : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ q, 0 ≤ f q) →
    ((∀ᵐ x : ℝ, IsApproximable f x) ↔
      ¬ Summable fun q : ℕ ↦ (Nat.totient q : ℝ) * f q / q) := by
  sorry

/-- It is easy to prove that divergence of the series follows from approximability almost
everywhere (the Borel–Cantelli lemma). -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_999.variants.easy_direction (f : ℕ → ℝ) (hf : ∀ q, 0 ≤ f q)
    (h : ∀ᵐ x : ℝ, IsApproximable f x) :
    ¬ Summable fun q : ℕ ↦ (Nat.totient q : ℝ) * f q / q := by
  sorry

/-- Erdős [Er64b] proved the conjecture in the special case when $f(q)q$ is bounded. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_999.variants.erdos (f : ℕ → ℝ) (hf : ∀ q, 0 ≤ f q)
    (hb : ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ q, f q * q ≤ C) :
    (∀ᵐ x : ℝ, IsApproximable f x) ↔
      ¬ Summable fun q : ℕ ↦ (Nat.totient q : ℝ) * f q / q := by
  sorry

end Erdos999

reformulations.difference: The source asks for infinitely many solutions (p, q) with (p, q) = 1 (KM20: infinitely many reduced fractions a/q). The Lean definition instead asks for infinitely many denominators q > 0 that admit some coprime numerator p: `{q : ℕ | 0 < q ∧ ∃ p : ℤ, Int.gcd p q = 1 ∧ |x - p / q| < f q / q}.Infinite`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For fixed q > 0 the inequality |x − p/q| < f(q)/q is |qx − p| < f(q). Only finitely many integers p satisfy it; they lie in [⌊qx − f q⌋, ⌈qx + f q⌉]. So the solution set in ℤ × ℕ has finite fibres over q, and it is infinite iff its projection onto q is infinite. Reduced fractions a/q with q ≥ 1 correspond one-to-one to coprime pairs. I proved this in Lean: `IsApproximable f x ↔ {pq : ℤ × ℕ | 0 < pq.2 ∧ Int.gcd pq.1 pq.2 = 1 ∧ |x - pq.1 / pq.2| < f pq.2 / pq.2}.Infinite`. The proof depends only on the standard axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

reformulations.difference: KM20 states the theorem with the non-strict inequality |α − a/q| ≤ ψ(q)/q, for α ∈ [0,1], with ψ defined on the positive integers, and writes the condition as Σ = ∞. The Lean differs in five places: (1) it uses the strict inequality, as erdosproblems.com and Erdős do; (2) it uses `∀ᵐ x : ℝ` (Lebesgue measure on all of ℝ); (3) it takes f : ℕ → ℝ with a nonnegativity hypothesis, and f 0 is included; (4) it writes divergence as `¬ Summable`; (5) it wraps the settled statement as `answer(True) ↔ …`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (i) Strict vs non-strict: A_< ⊆ A_≤, and A_≤ \ A_< lies in the countable set {a/q ± ψ(q)/q}, which is null. So one set has full (or zero) measure iff the other does. (ii) Proved in Lean: IsApproximable f (x+1) ↔ IsApproximable f x, via p ↦ p ± q, which preserves gcd with q. So the exceptional set is 1-periodic, and it is null in ℝ iff it is null in [0,1]. (iii) The terms φ(q)f(q)/q are ≥ 0 and the q = 0 term is 0. So `¬ Summable` holds iff the partial sums tend to +∞; this is `not_summable_iff_tendsto_nat_atTop_of_nonneg`, checked in Lean. (iv) IsApproximable requires q > 0, so f 0 plays no role. (v) `answer(True) ↔ P` is `True ↔ P`, i.e. P. Together with the easy Borel–Cantelli direction (Σ < ∞ ⟹ almost every α is non-approximable, and ℝ has positive measure), the Lean `↔` is exactly the source's 'is equivalent to'.

reformulations.difference: [Er64b] states the sharper special case for a bounded sequence ε_q ≥ 0, with inequality |α − p/q| < ε_q/q² and series Σ ε_q φ(q)/q². The displayed inequality is an image in the scan and was inferred from the series and from the convergent corollary with 1/(2n²). The Lean instead uses f(q) = ε_q/q and the hypothesis `∃ C, ∀ q, f q * q ≤ C`, following erdosproblems.com's phrasing 'f(q)q is bounded'.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Substitute ε_q = f(q)·q. Then ε_q/q² = f(q)/q and Σ ε_q φ(q)/q² = Σ φ(q) f(q)/q. Since f ≥ 0, 'ε_q bounded' is the same as an upper bound f(q)q ≤ C, which forces C ≥ 0 because f 0 * 0 = 0. Conversely, every bounded ε_q ≥ 0 gives such an f with f(q) = ε_q/q. Both sides assert the full necessary-and-sufficient equivalence.

review.notes:
No misformalization found. Main points:

1. erdosproblems.com/999 says 'f: ℕ → ℕ', and every revision on the history page says the same. This is a slip on the website. Erdős [Er64b, p. 60] states the Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture for 'an arbitrary sequence of non-negative numbers ε_q', and KM20 uses ψ: ℕ → ℝ≥0. With ℕ-valued f, the website's own remark about the case 'f(q)q bounded' would be trivial, since f(q) = 0 for q > C. The Lean (f : ℕ → ℝ with f ≥ 0) and its docstring (ℝ≥0) follow the primary sources. The Lean statement implies the website's literal ℕ-valued version, and both are true. I don't count this as a defect. Maintainers could tell the website.

2. Attribution in the docstring of `erdos_999.variants.erdos`: 'Erdős [Er64b] proved … when f(q)q is bounded' matches the website and Erdős's own claim in [Er64b]. There he says the proof 'has not yet been published', and that it gives the bounded-ε_q case. KM20 (introduction) credits the published proof of the ψ(q) = O(1/q) case to Erdős (1970) and then Vaaler (1978). This is a historical nuance only; the mathematics is unaffected, and the statement is true (Vaaler 1978, and KM20).

3. Lean checks (scratch files in /workspace/review):
   - `IsApproximable` elaborates to real division `↑p / ↑q` and `f q / ↑q`, with `Int.gcd p ↑q = 1`.
   - `∀ᵐ` is w.r.t. `volume` on ℝ.
   - The q = 0 series term is 0.
   - `f = 0` makes nothing approximable, so both sides of the main `↔` are false.
   - Proved: coprime-pair counting ⟺ denominator counting.
   - Proved: 1-periodicity of `IsApproximable`.
   - Proved: `¬ Summable` ⟺ the partial sums tend to infinity.

4. Status is consistent. The website says PROVED ('solved in the affirmative'), and teorth/erdosproblems says 'proved'. The file has `research solved` with `answer(True)`, a `textbook` easy direction (Borel–Cantelli), and `research solved` for the bounded case. No formal_proof is recorded, and I found no known Lean proof: there is no Erdos999.lean at the path I tried in plby/lean-proofs.

5. The live erdosproblems.com pages were blocked by a Cloudflare challenge. I used the Wayback snapshots of 2026-07-09. The file was added on 2026-09-21.
